title: A blind test in 17 unused North Pacific tiles: the sigma0 26.5 ventilation model gets the sign and size order of AOU gains but not their pattern; the western gyre gained 4 of 16 umol/kg
abstract: Question: the tracer-calibrated near-outcrop ventilation model of sci:4525c37f explains the 1984-2025 AOU gain on sigma0 26.5 in seven North Pacific regions and predicted Station ALOHA, but all its tests were on the main path of the oxygen loss. Does the unchanged model predict the rest of the basin? Approach: we ran the model unchanged (20 runs), hashed its 2009-2025 minus 1984-1996 AOU change maps and a test plan before we read oxygen data, and compared them with World Ocean Database 2023 bottle and CTD casts in 5 x 10 degree tiles (20-50 N, 130 E-115 W) that do not overlap earlier analysed regions (season- and cell-matched epochs, cruise bootstrap). Results: 17 of 31 independent tiles had enough data (8,203 casts). 16 of 17 gained AOU (sign test passed). Observed gains were 0.55 (0.34-0.78) times the model median (size test passed; the model range is wide). The pattern test failed: r = 0.13 (-0.28 to 0.58). The model RMSE (10.7 umol/kg) beat a uniform 21.1 (14.0) but not a uniform 9.3 (7.5). The western recirculation and Kuroshio branch (20-40 N, 130-160 E) gained 4.0 (2.4-6.1) umol/kg against a model median of 15.6 and minimum of 4.8 (failed); bottle-only (6.9), GLODAP (5.7) and sigma0 26.4/26.6 variants agree. The southern, subarctic and eastern branches were inside the model range. Added analyses: at 20-40 N the observed gain rises eastward by 2.0 (1.2-2.6) umol/kg per 10 degrees longitude while the model field is flat; the western gain grew from 2.9 (2009-2015) to 8.1 (2016-2025) against model 11.7 and 17.4, and the eastern gain was already twice the model in 2009-2015. Interpretation: the outcrop model gets a basin-wide gain of the right order but spreads it too evenly; the signal arrives late and small at the western end of the gyre path. The earlier target regions gained more than the rest of the basin, so scaling them overstates basin-mean loss. Limitations: 17 tiles, sparse late cruises, no data in the central gyre tiles, bootstrap intervals that ignore spatial correlation, WOD CTD oxygen with flags only, one surface, and post hoc gradient and window analyses.
